v.why: Replacing a learnable 3x3 conv on the output edge with parameter-free pooling costs accuracy (runs 95, 100), whereas replacing weaker ops costs less or helps.
Swapping a 3x3 conv for a skip loses representational capacity (runs 71, 78), while replacing other ops is near neutral.
Replacing an identity path to the output with pooling blurs features and hurts (runs 93, 98).
Upgrading a pooling edge to a conv adds learnable capacity, giving a larger gain than upgrading edges that already hold a conv (runs 54, 56, 60).
Replacing a non-learnable pooling edge with a 3x3 conv gives a big gain (runs 34, 37), unlike swaps from conv1x1 or skip.
A conv replacing pooling gains more than conv replacing other ops (runs 14, 20).
Replacing a parameter-free skip with a conv consistently helps across datasets (runs 13, 16, 17).
Replacing skip with a 3x3 conv adds capacity and helps more than replacing other ops (runs 43, 47, 49).
Replacing pooling at the input edge with a conv gives gains on all datasets (runs 4, 5), more than replacing an existing conv.
Removing a skip edge matters less than removing a conv edge, so the edit hurts less or helps (run 83), though other skip parents show mixed results.
